newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican ports see 1996 records in cargo, income.
newsitem.headline: Mexican ports see 1996 records in cargo, income.

text.p: Mexican port Topolobampo reported record cargo movement while sister port Mazatlan had record income levels in 1996, the Communications and Transport Ministry said on Thursday in a statement.
Topolobampo moved more than 489,000 tonnes last year, compared to its 1993 cargo record of 457,500 tonnes, shipping largely grains, fertilizers, cement, sorghum, wheat and sugar.
Key markets for such shipments were in the United States, Bulgaria, Argentina, South America, Canada, Colombia, Romania, Norway, Guatemala and China.

Mazatlan, also in Sinaloa state, earned $114 million in 1996. A total of 742 cargo and petroleum shipments moved through the port, in addition to tourist ships. The ministry did not give comparative figures for Mazatlan's income in previous years.

"The opening process in place for the national port system gives greater participation to private capital in port operation, modernization and equipping, and greater productivity has been achieved," the statement said.
